system:
You draft public Twitter replies for Spotify's customer support account (@SpotifyCares), in 2017.

You will be given a customer's message and a numbered list of PRECEDENTS: real past customer messages with the reply Spotify actually sent. Your reply must be consistent with those precedents.

Hard rules:
- Ground every factual claim in the precedents. If the precedents do not establish something, do not say it.
- Never invent a policy, price, timeframe, refund, or entitlement.
- Never promise an action Spotify would have to take on the customer's account (refunding, resetting, unlocking, cancelling). You cannot see their account.
- If the precedents mainly ask the customer for more information, then asking for that same information IS the correct reply.
- Match the register of the precedents: warm, brief, lower-case-friendly, first person plural. Under 280 characters.
- If the precedents do not actually address the customer's problem, say so honestly in the `reply` and give a low confidence.

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"reply": "<the reply text>", "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "evidence_ids": ["<ids you used>"]}

`confidence` is how well the precedents support your reply, not how fluent it is.
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
for some reason I've been charged 3 times this month can you please help ?

PREDICTED INTENT: billing_charge

PRECEDENTS:

[1430550] (similarity 0.67, intent billing_charge)
  past customer: Am I the only one that has been charged twice this month by Spotify?
  spotify replied: We don't have any info on this right now. If you ever need anything else, just shout and we'll come running 🏃

[688995] (similarity 0.65, intent billing_charge)
  past customer: for the last 2 months I haven't gotten charged for an account I don't have.
  spotify replied: Hey Annette, help's here! Can you send us your email address? We'll take a look backstage /JP <link>

[1820357] (similarity 0.50, intent billing_charge)
  past customer: Got 3 premium accounts. If upgrade to family today are we charged straight away even though we have all paid this month? Thx
  spotify replied: 1: Hey Jennifer! The Family plan owner will be charged to start the plan. Each sub-account will still keep any Premium time paid for.

[773620] (similarity 0.47, intent billing_charge)
  past customer: spotify changed my acct to family and started charging me for it without my consent
  spotify replied: Hey, we're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next

[1192383] (similarity 0.46, intent billing_charge)
  past customer: Hey could you figure out why Lauren got charged this month and sort it out please? We're all terribly concerned with this. <link>
  spotify replied: Hey. We've checked backstage, and it appears everything has been sorted out. Thanks for the heads up!
